history.notes: Adds the `ONSCREEN_SELECTION` room binding that 3.0.2 declined: a third connection named **Onscreen Navigator**, id 7500, type 7, facing 6, consumer False, all three source flags False. Declaring it is what makes a device eligible for a room's **On-Screen Device** row in Connections, so the NVR can now be offered there beside the CORE processors. Daniel asked for it, reaffirmed it after the refusal, and authorized shipping it into his own test house — this release is that experiment, run on real hardware instead of argued on paper. · Every field value is cited, not guessed. They come from Control4's own DriverWorks section for a receiver with an onscreen binding (snap-one/docs-driverworks-api, `source/includes/19_media_management_miscellaneous/_1-Receiver_with_Onscreen_Binding.md`), including the three source flags rendered explicitly as False — the shape the official example shows. The build now emits those flags whenever a manifest declares any of them, so the render matches the documented example rather than approximating it. · The precondition is unmet and stated as such. That same section makes a video path the condition of the binding: the room must also be able to select the device as its **video endpoint**. This driver is a source feeding a matrix and can never be one, so whether Composer lists it and whether Director accepts the assignment is **unproven**. Nothing here promises it works. If it does not appear in the room's list, that is the documentation asserting itself, not a defect. Selecting **Security Cameras** as the room's **video source** remains the supported, field-proven path for cameras on a TV and is untouched by this release. · The risk if a room does take it: the room enters navigation mode and forwards every arrow, `ENTER`, `BACK`, `CANCEL` and `GUIDE` to the bound driver until navigation exits. This driver has no control path — no socket, no credentials, a proxy handler that does nothing — so it swallows them and nothing on screen moves. The remedy is one step: clear it out of the room's On-Screen Device row and the keys return to the CORE. The guide's Program the project section now says all of this in place of the flat refusal it carried in 3.0.2, and it is said in the two other places a dealer would actually be standing: Start here names the new binding as an experiment, because you meet it in Composer's Connections tree before you ever reach the Programming section, and Troubleshoot leads with it — a room whose arrows, ENTER and BACK went dead is this release's one new failure mode, and the person hunting it will open Troubleshoot, not the release notes. Start here also dropped a single-binding "only job" line that the third connection made false. The tests that guarded the refusal were flipped to pin the binding's exact rendered block instead, and a new case reads the rendered guide itself and fails if any of those three sections stops saying it. A new case pins what did *not* change: the binding added no command, no variable and no event, so this is still not a controllable device. · Note the cost of reversal, on the record now rather than discovered later: id 7500 is published the moment this ships, and taking the binding back out in a later release retires a published id, which breaks any dealer programming bound to it. The Update Sentinel will refuse that push until the release notes carry its retire-authorization marker — the literal `ID`/`RETIRE`/`OK` line defined in `tools/qa-id-stability.mjs`, spelled as one phrase, which this entry deliberately does NOT spell because this release retires nothing. Pulling the binding is therefore a deliberate, documented act, and that is the price of finding out whether it works.

The guide now states plainly why this source can never be the room's On-Screen Device, and why that is not a missing feature. Control4's own driver documentation (DriverWorks, *Receiver with Onscreen Binding*) makes a video path the condition of that binding: the room must be able to select the same device as its **video endpoint**. That row holds an endpoint — the controller pushing Navigator out its HDMI, or an AV receiver. This driver is the opposite end of the wire: a provider that hands video to the matrix. Bound there anyway, the room would enter navigation mode and forward every arrow, ENTER and BACK to a driver with no control path; the keys would vanish and the TV would show the same camera grid it already shows. Adding a room-binding connection to make it appear in that list was designed, costed, and declined — an entry that swallows the remote is a fabrication, and a wrong binding id is expensive to retire once it is fielded. · The camera-on-TV workflow is pointed at the row that already works: select **Security Cameras** as the room's **video source**. That path is field-proven, and the doc now says outright that no Control4 UI renders on this feed — no menus, no cursor, no per-camera picker — so nobody goes hunting for one. · Tests pin the refusal rather than trusting it: the rendered package is now asserted to carry exactly two connections, no `ONSCREEN_SELECTION` class, nothing in the 7000–7999 room-binding range, no type-7 connection, and the unchanged **HDMI OUT** output — plus the standing truth that this driver declares no commands, no device events and no variables of its own. Landing the declined binding turns those cases red.

Certification pass: this driver was read end to end against its own manifest and code — every name checked for a single spelling across the manifest, the code and this guide, and every claim in the documentation verified against what the code does rather than what it intended. · The guide gained the Program the project section the documentation contract requires. It says plainly that there is nothing on this driver to program — a display-only source declares no commands, no device events and no variables, so any of those here would be fiction — and then shows where the automation actually lives: the room selects the source, the matrix routes the HDMI, and a doorbell-to-theater recipe demonstrates the shape. A stale reference to the package's internal version number was removed rather than left to go stale again. · Two latent release blockers, both found by trying to release: a test pinned the running build's version to the literal 3.0.0, and the golden-artifact comparison rewrote this driver's minimum OS version because it happened to read the same as its driver version. Either one would have failed the first patch release. Both are fixed at the root, so this driver can be updated normally from here.

Factory integration of the field-proven hand-built driver, crediting the v1-v3 lineage: v2 was proven routing video on an AVPro Edge MX Pro matrix, and v2's blank icon was root-caused to the state-block-vs-flat-ladder Navigator bug and fixed in v3. · Same display-only contract: a satellite source proxy exposing one HDMI OUT binding (classes HDMI + STEREO) for the UniFi NVR G2 live-view output, with the branded aperture-tile Navigator icon ladder rendered as a flat ladder (never state blocks). · New over the hand-built lineage: self-update from the IntegrateIT channel, the packaged Documentation tab, and static + runtime + golden QA — plus the name-equals-filename controller:// URL validator this driver contributed to the whole fleet. · xmlVersion bumped to 4 (Control4 fact #5 - a re-release must bump the integer version or Navigators keep the stale icon).
